boundary_note: Bounded first pass for all four frozen records in Longstreet's Tidewater Operations [March-April 1863]. Preserve per-engagement dates: Fort Anderson March 13–15, Washington March 30–April 20, Suffolk (Norfleet House) April 13–15 and Suffolk (Fort Huger/Hill's Point) April 11–May 4, 1863. VA030's frozen interval lies inside VA031's, and both frozen casualty texts refer to one 1,160 siege total; their quantities must not be added. The live NPS campaign dates do not replace any battle interval. Opening personnel and exact effective command boundaries remain unresolved. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength); the frozen battle-level 45,000 total is shared by VA030 and VA031 and its scope is not stated. No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Divisions (45,000 total), shared with VA031; the live field reads zero. NPS says the Union works were manned by 25,000 men against Longstreet's 20,000. Peck says 15,000 of Longstreet's corps were on the Blackwater and 15,000 between Petersburg and the river after late February, and that on the 15th the force between Suffolk and the West Branch was reported at 10,000.
claims.rationale: Siege-level, pre-advance and sector figures differ in scope and source; none is adopted as a matched opening strength for April 13–15. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Inconclusive and the live result Indecisive. NPS says the Mount Washington was crippled on April 14 and that on April 15 the Union batteries drove the Confederates out of the Norfleet House position. Peck says the Mount Washington was riddled, disabled and grounded, and that on the 15th four 20-pounder rifles were dismounted and the Norfleet battery silenced. French's report of the 15th does not mention that battery being silenced.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. Whether French's and Peck's accounts of the 15th describe the same guns is not established.

open_questions: Longstreet's and Hood's reports, the navy reports of April 14 and Getty's report remain deferred; the engagement's own casualties are unknown.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Foster's, D. H. Hill's, Peck's and French's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XVIII, are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. The compiler's footnote is counted with the Foster selection, and Longstreet's indorsement with French's report, for the effort ceiling; neither is treated as independent corroboration. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
